title: Ethiopian Spiced Rice Pudding
community: Urban Ethiopia — the spiced milk dessert
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Spiced Rice Pudding — short-grain rice slowly cooked in milk with Ethiopian honey, cardamom, cinnamon, and rose water. The Ethiopian version of rice pudding — warmer-spiced than European versions, sweetened with mountain honey rather than sugar.
longDesc: Ethiopian rice pudding is the warm comfort dessert of urban Ethiopia — the familiar rice-in-milk preparation transformed by the Ethiopian spice tradition into something distinctly its own. The cardamom and rose water speak to the Arab culinary influence on Ethiopian Muslim communities.
ingredients: // Garnish: pinch of ground cinnamon, chopped pistachios (optional)
steps: Rinse rice. Combine with water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat. Simmer 10 minutes until water is absorbed.
Add milk, honey, sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, for 20—25 minutes.
The pudding should be thick and creamy — the rice very soft.
Garnish with a pinch of cinnamon.
chefTips: Stir frequently — rice pudding sticks easily.
The pudding thickens significantly on cooling — remove from heat slightly looser than desired.
Rose water is the finishing touch that gives it its distinctive Middle-Eastern-Ethiopian character.
commonMistakes: Removing from heat too thick — becomes solid when cold.
cookingScience: Short-grain rice releases much more amylopectin (a highly branched starch) than long-grain rice during cooking — this starch thickens the milk into the characteristic pudding consistency. The milk proteins (casein) also partially denature during the long cooking, contributing to the creamy texture.
servedWith: As a dessert warm or cold
For children as a nutritious dessert
reheating: Gently with a splash of milk.
culturalNote: Ethiopian spiced rice pudding is the sweet that Ethiopian mothers make for sick children — warm, gentle, and easy to eat. The cardamom and honey make it comforting in the same way that chicken soup is comforting in other cultures.
